With the obsession going around of RPGs with the Witcher 3, Elder Scrolls Online and Shooters still all the rage. I feel like we need to appreciate the underdogs of the gaming industry. I'm talking about those genres you like which haven't had any decent games released or any at all for the past few years.

I have only 2 off the top of my head:

Roller Coaster Simulators: For the span of around 10-14 years we didn't get anything all that great in terms of this genre. Now however everyone seems to be trying to create one. Just to name a few from the past few years: Coaster Crazy, NL2. RCTW, Coaster Park Tycoon and Theme Parkitect.

Train Simulators: Right now we have two main contestants for the best Train Simulator game on the market: Railworks: A game with overpriced DLC which even though it's cheaper than a real model train set is still unbelievalbly expensive. I've probably dropped around £200-£300 on this game. Thankfully any routes, reskins and new trains are often free and not stuck behind DRM. Did I also mention the horrible optimization and cut-paste creation of this every year? Trainz: A New Era: I considered this game but from what I've seen it's a gigantic disappointment. I saw the trailer and I really hoped it was good. But nope it looks horrific. The worst part is all modding is stuck behind DRM. Reskins, Routes and new trains are always hosted on the developers website and they insist you create an account AND activate a valid key to even access and download mods from there. This infuriates me to no end. This genre desperately needs a well made game from honest train lovers who want to make a genuinely good train game and not focus on the money.

What do you think? What hidden gems do you think need more games/recognition?
What gaming genre do you want to get more recognition and more games released?

I was honestly hoping the runaway success of XCOM would have led to some changes in the way publishers approached games. The Bureau was their big project, meant to bring the franchise into the 21st century as a shooter. Enemy Unknown was, while obviously well-made and having a decent budget, not expected to be the one that would define how XCOM went forward. Now, The Bureau is a footnote and XCOM got an expansion and will have a sequel, because one of them was a mediocre shooter and the other was true to the series and provided something that the market wasn't utterly oversaturated with.

Apparently nobody's noticed the reason for this success, yet.

Honestly, at the time of The Bureaus announcement gaming was in a fanatic place with shooters. BioShock had come out. Borderlands was a juggernaut for 2k and it seemed like a every shooter was hitting gold for 2k. So I feel it's easy to see why try were pushing the FPS hard. However, as you said, it bombed horribly and the TBS game had a nice bit of success. I believe XCOM 2 coming to PC only is a way for them to see if they just got lucky, or if this franchise has some serious legs on all platforms.

I haven't seen a good city building game that's set in the classic period in a long time. I enjoyed the hell out of Impression's City Building series; Caesar, Pharaoh, Zeus, Emperor. I'd love to see someone utilize modern graphics and processor capabilities to remake something like that.

Also, historic sims - like the Silent Hunter series before it went to shit.

I want some more arpgs. I mean I'll preface this by saying dark souls is pretty much crack for me, but honestly it's been a pretty successful genre in the past, and many critically acclaimed games have come from the genre. Personally I really appreciate the mixing of solid game play mechanics with jrpgs stylization. Aka can't wait for kingdom hearts 3

I would like to see more real time strategy games like StaCraft or C&C Generals. I guess those types of games are no longer popular. Too bad. Looking forward to the protoss campaign for StarCraft 2 now.

I'd like to see more RPG games in the way of Sid Meier's Pirates and Mount & Blade. The kind where you're playing as an ordinary individual traversing across an active world map with lots of NPC action going on around you, recruiting others to your party, participating to some extent in an economy that changes over the course of a playthrough, with goals that are open-ended, and a plot that is either very basic or not there at all.

Games like Homeworld (Scifi 3D RTS)

Homeworld is a true 3D RTS, there have been only a handful of games that even TRIED to follow it's lead (Nexus, Hegemonia, Flotilla) but none of them really came close, even the sequel wasn't as good.

Games like Dungeon Keeper (RTS with autonomous entities and objective-based scenarios)

Until this year Dungeon Keeper was a genre unto itself, the only games in it were DK1 and 2 and Evil Genius (which, while fun, has serious issues). Attempts to join the genre by games like Dungeons and Impire were failures; the games either lacked the open nature of DK development or focused on new gameplay elements that detracted from the experience. This year War of the Overlord came out and, while not perfect, many have enjoyed it, Dungeons 2 came out and surprised everyone by not sucking (WWWAAAAT???) and another game (Dwelvers) is on the way promising to offer more. Still, these are 3 games, not 10. I want more.

Games like Star Trek: Bridge Commander or Artemis (Capitol ship simulators)

We finally have the technology to reproduce the Star Trek bridge experience well but there are literally two games in this genre and one of them is MP only. The Independence War games (all both of them) offered a more sim-heavy SP experience but they are old as hell. I would love more games giving control of giant spaceships.

Games like Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss (openworld first person RPG dungeon crawler)

Ultima Underworld is probably my favorite game and even now, 20+ years later, no game has offered a more immersive dungeoncrawling experience. Sure Legend of Grimrock was cool, but that was a love letter to the games that came before UU, especially Dungeon Master. Ultima Underworld was full glorious 2.5, you could look up and down and jump and swim and FUCKING FLY (you cant even do that in TES games anymore). Other than the sequel and the Arkane Studios homage Arx Fatalis, though, this genre has been dead. Some of the original devs are working on a spiritual remake (Underworld Ascendant, which made its Kickstarter goal but is still accepting donations) but that's one fucking game. C'mon devs. Pls.

Games like Syndicate and Syndicate Wars (third person action strategy/tactics/management)

I don't mean the competent but wholly unnecessary 2012 reboot, I mean the original. It could be argued that Dawn of War 2 is pretty similar, and that is true... but one game is not enough. Ok, there was Krater and Darkspore also... but those sucked.

Games like Descent:Freespace 1 and 2 (Plot/mission based space combat sims)

Kickstarter has revived the long nascent space combat sim with Elite: Dangerous and Star Citizen and (someday) No Man's Sky, but none of these games seem to be offering what I loved the most about the genre back when it was big: a big space opera story set against the backdrop of intergalactic war. Classics like Xwing, TieFighter, the Freespace games and even 'lesser' titles like Tachyon and Darkstar One were effective at making you feel like part of a big story and that is totally absent from the only recent release in the genre (Elite:Dangerous). Personally I hope they license that engine for someone else to make a story-rich game with.

There's more and more but this is already too long of a post.
